text: The migration of listing and asset_sale is delivered with S5 rwb-asset, and RWB-P1-DM006-APP migrates only the appraisal acceptance to valuation_ext, keeps the DP06 read path and holds the DP06 cutover gate, validating asset_key links against the rwb-asset contract fake.
why: The two tables are not in the P1 ownership rows, so no wave-4 story could otherwise name their schema and the AC1 payload would have no owner.
read: Context pack P1 ownership rows (18 tables, listing and asset_sale absent); RWB-DM-006 Data table; DP-05 read path for DP06; R5.5 DP-11 contract mock.
confirm: Data architect and the S5 rwb-asset technical owner at the wave-4 contract review
impact: AC1 keeps the legacy wording and adds the rwb-asset contract mock as its first Given; no C dependency is recorded because the contract is a fake.

text: The legacy listing, sale instruction and appraisal acceptance tables stay read-only for the retention class of their record class in retention_rule, and the ten clean days of AC3 run inside that period.
why: AC3 names a retention period but no source gives its value; the Workbench retention rule is the only retention control that exists after the realignment.
read: RWB-DM-006 AC3; FSD P1 A2.17; TSD P1 T3.5.
confirm: Data steward and data product owner at the cutover sign-off
impact: The cutover gate uses the retention class rather than a new period; the value is confirmed in the cutover plan, not in code.

text: A migration batch is described by the existing LOV-FRESHNESS values (LOADED, STALE) plus the AC3 gate (extracted, loaded, reconciled, signed off, cut over, held), and no new list of values is added.
why: No source names migration states, and a new list would put a business value in code without a reference data row.
read: RWB-DM-006 AC1 and AC3; TSD P1 T3.7 and T3.8.
impact: Section 9 stays descriptive; nothing is added to the lists of values.

text: Legacy AC2 (reconcile the business keys, the REC-05 step) and its test case TC-DM-006-02 sit with the reconciliation deliverable of the same legacy key, so RWB-P1-DM006-APP owns AC1 and AC3 only and keeps TC-DM-006-01, TC-DM-006-03 and TC-DM-006-04.
why: The work package assigns AC1 and AC3 to this story, and R5.5 DP-05 puts REC-05 in the daily reconciliation of the service, not in a cutover migration.
read: WP B2-P1-005 story line (acs AC1, AC3); RWB-DM-006 AC2; FSD P1 A2.11 (REC-05).
impact: AC2 and TC-DM-006-02 are not restated here, and no AC or TC is duplicated across the two stories.
